relationships.subject: sphenopalatine ganglion
relationships.evidence_quote: Evidence suggests that the SPG contributes to meningeal vasodilation and neurogenic inflammation by releasing vasoactive neuropeptides such as CGRP, substance P, and nitric oxide

relationships.subject: SPG block
relationships.evidence_quote: By doing so, they attenuate the neurogenic inflammation and vascular changes that contribute to headache pathophysiology

key_findings: Review: SPG blocks and stimulation are options for refractory migraine and cluster headache; SPG stimulation aborted 67% of cluster attacks vs 7% sham.
SPG blocks are proposed to reduce release of CGRP and substance P and attenuate neurogenic inflammation.
